newsitem.title: FRANCE: Thomson-CSF up as privatisation nears.
newsitem.headline: Thomson-CSF up as privatisation nears.

text.p: Shares in Thomson-CSF were up five francs, or 3.6 percent, at 145.30 at 1150 GMT on the view that the privatisation of Thomson SA has entered the final phase, brokers said on Monday.
"This rise is due to the approaching privatisation. We're entering the last lap, with the deadline for offers coming up on September 15," said analyst Antoine Nodet at Dupont Denant.

The announcement on Friday by one of the prospective bidders, Alcatel Alsthom, that its GEC Alsthom venture with GEC is studying a merger with state-owned Framatome has stirred speculation about the Thomson sale.
Analysts were divided as to whether Alcatel's move on Framatome, a nuclear reactor builder, would make it more or less likely to win the bid for Thomson over rival Lagardere Group.

While some say the two deals would represent a cumbersome diversification for Alcatel, others say control of Framatome -- with its eight billion francs of cash -- and the contribution from GEC would help Alcatel finance a bid for Thomson.
The government is expected to sell Thomson, which comprises Thomson-CSF and Thomson Multimedia, before the end of the year.

Nodet said he continues to recommend shares in Thomson-CSF which he values at 160 francs. Another analyst said he expects the successful bidder for Thomson will make an attractive offer to Thomson-CSF's minority shareholders.
